## 1. This week's analysis

Worked example from [Week 05: Annotation and genomic
ranges](https://sr320.github.io/course-fish546-2026/assignments/05-annotation-ranges.html).
I locate two fish 12S eDNA primer pairs (MiFish-U and Riaz 12S) on the
Chinook salmon (*Oncorhynchus tshawytscha*) mitogenome and use the NCBI
annotation to find out which gene each amplicon falls in.

**Platform:** laptop (macOS). **Software:** R with Bioconductor
`Biostrings` and `GenomicRanges`; package versions are printed by
`sessionInfo()` at the end of this section.

**Outputs:**

-   [`output/week05/amplicon-annotation.csv`](../output/week05/amplicon-annotation.csv)
-   [`output/week05/amplicons.bed`](../output/week05/amplicons.bed)

### 1.1 Setup and download

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
# Install once if needed (not run on every render):
# if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
# BiocManager::install(c("Biostrings", "GenomicRanges"))

library(Biostrings)
library(GenomicRanges)

data_dir <- "../data/week05"
out_dir  <- "../output/week05"
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(out_dir,  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

accession <- "NC_002980.1"   # genome build = accession + version
fasta_file <- file.path(data_dir, paste0(accession, ".fasta"))
gff_file   <- file.path(data_dir, paste0(accession, ".gff3"))

if (!file.exists(fasta_file)) {
  download.file(
    paste0("https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?",
           "db=nuccore&rettype=fasta&retmode=text&id=", accession),
    fasta_file, quiet = TRUE)
}
if (!file.exists(gff_file)) {
  download.file(
    paste0("https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sviewer/viewer.cgi?",
           "db=nuccore&report=gff3&id=", accession),
    gff_file, quiet = TRUE)
}

genome <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file)
names(genome)
width(genome)   # expect 16,644 bp, one circular sequence

# Use the bare accession.version as the sequence name so it matches GFF column 1
names(genome) <- accession
chinook <- genome[[1]]
```

### 1.2 Read the GFF

GFF3 is nine tab-separated columns, **1-based and inclusive** on both
ends.

```{r}
#| label: read-gff
gff_cols <- c("seqid", "source", "type", "start", "end",
              "score", "strand", "phase", "attributes")
gff <- read.delim(gff_file, header = FALSE, comment.char = "#",
                  col.names = gff_cols, quote = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

table(gff$type)

keep_types <- c("rRNA", "tRNA", "CDS", "D_loop")
feat <- gff[gff$type %in% keep_types, ]

# Pull product= out of the attributes column (URL-decode e.g. %2C)
get_attr <- function(x, key) {
  m <- regmatches(x, regexpr(paste0("(?<=", key, "=)[^;]+"), x, perl = TRUE))
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  out[grepl(paste0(key, "="), x)] <- m
  vapply(out, function(s) if (is.na(s)) NA_character_ else URLdecode(s),
         character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
feat$product <- get_attr(feat$attributes, "product")
feat$product[feat$type == "D_loop"] <- "control region (D-loop)"

head(feat[, c("type", "start", "end", "strand", "product")], 10)
```

### 1.3 Build genomic ranges

`GRanges` is also **1-based, inclusive**, so GFF coordinates go in
unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: granges
features_gr <- GRanges(
  seqnames = feat$seqid,
  ranges   = IRanges(start = feat$start, end = feat$end),
  strand   = feat$strand,
  type     = feat$type,
  product  = feat$product
)
seqlengths(features_gr) <- setNames(length(chinook), accession)
isCircular(features_gr) <- setNames(TRUE, accession)

features_gr
table(features_gr$type)
```

### 1.4 Locate primers

Forward primers match the plus strand as written; reverse primers are
written 5'→3' on the minus strand, so I search for their reverse
complement. Up to 2 mismatches allowed.

```{r}
#| label: primers
primers <- data.frame(
  marker  = c("MiFish-U", "Riaz 12S"),
  forward = c("GTCGGTAAAACTCGTGCCAGC", "ACTGGGATTAGATACCCC"),
  reverse = c("CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTG", "TAGAACAGGCTCCTCTAG")
)

find_amplicon <- function(fwd, rev, subject, max_mm = 2, fixed = TRUE) {
  f_hit <- matchPattern(DNAString(fwd), subject,
                        max.mismatch = max_mm, fixed = fixed)
  r_hit <- matchPattern(reverseComplement(DNAString(rev)), subject,
                        max.mismatch = max_mm, fixed = fixed)
  stopifnot(length(f_hit) == 1, length(r_hit) == 1)
  data.frame(fwd_start = start(f_hit), fwd_end = end(f_hit),
             rev_start = start(r_hit), rev_end = end(r_hit),
             amp_start = start(f_hit), amp_end = end(r_hit))
}

amp_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(primers)), function(i)
  cbind(marker = primers$marker[i],
        find_amplicon(primers$forward[i], primers$reverse[i], chinook))))
amp_tab$length_bp <- amp_tab$amp_end - amp_tab$amp_start + 1
amp_tab
# Expected: MiFish-U 1,279-1,496 (218 bp); Riaz 12S 1,473-1,614 (142 bp)

amplicons_gr <- GRanges(
  seqnames = accession,
  ranges   = IRanges(amp_tab$amp_start, amp_tab$amp_end),
  strand   = "+",
  marker   = amp_tab$marker
)
amplicons_gr
```

### 1.5 Annotate amplicons by overlap

```{r}
#| label: overlap
hits <- findOverlaps(amplicons_gr, features_gr, ignore.strand = TRUE)

annot <- data.frame(
  marker        = amplicons_gr$marker[queryHits(hits)],
  amp_start     = start(amplicons_gr)[queryHits(hits)],
  amp_end       = end(amplicons_gr)[queryHits(hits)],
  feature_type  = features_gr$type[subjectHits(hits)],
  product       = features_gr$product[subjectHits(hits)],
  feature_start = start(features_gr)[subjectHits(hits)],
  feature_end   = end(features_gr)[subjectHits(hits)],
  feature_strand = as.character(strand(features_gr))[subjectHits(hits)]
)
annot

write.csv(annot, file.path(out_dir, "amplicon-annotation.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Is each amplicon fully contained in its feature?
within <- findOverlaps(amplicons_gr, features_gr, type = "within",
                       ignore.strand = TRUE)
data.frame(marker  = amplicons_gr$marker[queryHits(within)],
           within  = features_gr$product[subjectHits(within)])

# How much do the two amplicons overlap?
ov <- pintersect(amplicons_gr[1], amplicons_gr[2])
ov
width(ov)
```

### 1.6 Export BED

BED is **0-based, half-open**: subtract 1 from the start, keep the end.
This shift is the most common coordinate bug in genomics.

```{r}
#| label: bed
bed <- data.frame(
  chrom      = as.character(seqnames(amplicons_gr)),
  chromStart = start(amplicons_gr) - 1,
  chromEnd   = end(amplicons_gr),
  name       = amplicons_gr$marker,
  score      = 0,
  strand     = as.character(strand(amplicons_gr))
)
bed

write.table(bed, file.path(out_dir, "amplicons.bed"), sep = "\t",
            quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)

# Sanity check: BED length (end - start) equals GRanges width
stopifnot(all(bed$chromEnd - bed$chromStart == width(amplicons_gr)))
```

### 1.7 Optional extension: Leray COI

The Leray primers contain IUPAC ambiguity codes (W, Y, R, N), so the
search uses `fixed = FALSE` to let them match any of their bases. I step
up the mismatch allowance until the forward primer matches.

```{r}
#| label: leray
leray_f <- "GGWACWGGWTGAACWGTWTAYCCYCC"
leray_r <- "TANACYTCNGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA"

for (mm in 0:5) {
  n <- length(matchPattern(DNAString(leray_f), chinook,
                           max.mismatch = mm, fixed = FALSE))
  cat("forward, max.mismatch =", mm, "->", n, "hit(s)\n")
  if (n > 0) { leray_mm <- mm; break }
}

leray_rev_hits <- matchPattern(reverseComplement(DNAString(leray_r)), chinook,
                               max.mismatch = leray_mm, fixed = FALSE)
leray_rev_hits

leray_amp <- find_amplicon(leray_f, leray_r, chinook,
                           max_mm = leray_mm, fixed = FALSE)
leray_amp$length_bp <- leray_amp$amp_end - leray_amp$amp_start + 1
leray_amp

leray_gr <- GRanges(accession, IRanges(leray_amp$amp_start, leray_amp$amp_end))
leray_hits <- findOverlaps(leray_gr, features_gr, ignore.strand = TRUE)
features_gr[subjectHits(leray_hits)]
```

### 1.8 What to write

1.  **Accession and coordinate conventions.** I used `NC_002980.1`
    (accession + version 1). GFF3 is 1-based, inclusive; `GRanges` is
    1-based, inclusive (so GFF coordinates load unchanged); BED is
    0-based, half-open (start − 1, end unchanged).
2.  **Which gene, and how much overlap?** Both amplicons sit entirely
    within the 12S ribosomal RNA gene (1,055–2,001): MiFish-U at
    1,279–1,496 (218 bp) and Riaz 12S at 1,473–1,614 (142 bp). They
    overlap by `r width(ov)` bp (positions `r start(ov)`–`r end(ov)`),
    which is essentially where the MiFish-U reverse primer and the Riaz
    forward primer sit. So the two markers read mostly different,
    adjacent stretches of 12S, with Riaz 12S further 3'. *Extension:* the
    Leray COI forward primer needs 4 mismatches (even with IUPAC codes)
    before it hits Chinook; the amplicon is 6,821–7,185 (365 bp), inside
    cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (6,455–8,005).
3.  **What this shows and doesn't.** It shows where these primer
    sequences land on one Chinook reference mitogenome and which
    annotated gene those coordinates sit in. It doesn't show that the
    primers amplify in practice, how well they match other salmonids or
    other Chinook haplotypes (one reference, ≤2 mismatches is a string
    search, not PCR), or that the amplicon region discriminates species.
    Those need other genomes, alignments, or wet-lab data.
